verses.text: Now Jethro, the priest of Midian, Moise’ father-in-law, heard of all that Dumnezeu had done for Moise and for Israel his people, how the DOMNUL had brought Israel out of Egipt. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)
Jethro, Moise’ father-in-law, received Zipporah, Moise’ wife, after he had sent her away, (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)
and her two sons. The name of one son was Gershom, for Moise a zis, I have lived as a foreigner in a foreign țară.
The name of the other was Eliezer, for he a zis, My father’s Dumnezeu was my help and delivered me from Faraon’s sword. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)
Jethro, Moise’ father-in-law, came with Moise’ sons and his wife to Moise into the wilderness where he was encamped, at the Mountain of Dumnezeu. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)
He i-a zis lui Moise, I, your father-in-law Jethro, have come to you with your wife, and her two sons with her. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)
Moise went out to meet his father-in-law, and bowed and kissed him. They asked each other of their welfare, and they came into the tent. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)

Moise told his father-in-law all that the DOMNUL had done to Faraon and to the Egiptians for Israel’s sake, all the hardships that had come on them on the way, and how the DOMNUL delivered them. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)
Jethro rejoiced for all the să pleceodness which the DOMNUL had done to Israel, in that he had delivered them out of the mână of the Egiptians.
Jethro a zis, Blessed be the DOMNUL, who has delivered you out of the mână of the Egiptians, and out of the mână of Faraon; who has delivered the people from under the mână of the Egiptians.
Now I know that the DOMNUL is greater than all să pleceds because of the way that they treated people arrogantly.

Jethro, Moise’ father-in-law, took a burnt offering and sacrifices for Dumnezeu. Aaron came with all the elders of Israel, to eat bread with Moise’ father-in-law before Dumnezeu. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)
On the next day, Moise sat to judge the people, and the people stood around Moise from the morning to the evening. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)

When Moise’ father-in-law saw all that he did to the people, he a zis, What is this thing that you do for the people? Why do you sit alone, and all the people stand around you from morning to evening? (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)
Moise i-a zis lui his father-in-law, Because the people come to me to inquire of Dumnezeu. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)
When they have a matter, they come to me, and I judge between a man and his neighbor, and I make them know the statutes of Dumnezeu, and his laws. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)
Moise’ father-in-law i-a zis lui him, The thing that you do is not să pleceod.
You will surely wear away, both you, and this people that is with you; for the thing is too heavy for you. You are not able to perform it yourself alone. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)
Listen now to my voice. I will give you counsel, and Dumnezeu be with you. You represent the people before Dumnezeu, and bring the causes to Dumnezeu. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)
You shall teach them the statutes and the laws, and shall show them the way in which they must walk, and the work that they must do. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)

Moreover you shall provide out of all the people able men which fear Dumnezeu: men of truth, hating unjust gain; and place such over them, to be rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)

Let them judge the people at all times. It shall be that every great matter they shall bring to you, but every small matter they shall judge themselves. So shall it be easier for you, and they shall share the load with you. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)
If you will do this thing, and Dumnezeu commands you so, then you will be able to endure, and all these people also will să plece to their place in peace.
So Moise listened to the voice of his father-in-law, and did all that he had a zis. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)

Moise chose able men out of all Israel, and made them heads over the people, rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)
They judged the people at all times. They brought the hard cases to Moise, but every small matter they judged themselves. (text revizuit în limba română cu diacritice)
Moise let his father-in-law depart, and he went his way into his own țară.
